integrated_multimodal_description: Claymation plasticine stop-motion, handcrafted modelling clay with visible fingerprints and matte finish, photographed on a miniature practical set. Warm work light grazes the plank walls of a narrow farm dairy. A shallow recess is cut into the stone counter. Its low front lip overhangs just the rear edge of the small four-tile floor. The tiles extend forward in an exposed strip wider than the hoop pair, with clear sightlines over the lip to both hoop bases. A high back rim hides the tiles from the dry gallery. A fixed brass tap feeds the open front half. One lamp shelf pivots on a hinge bolted to the back rim: two sealed battery hoops above, a broad clay heel underneath, a dry right handle and a high thumb switch. The raised shelf leans against a stop. One rectangular oak block sits on edge on the dry right sill in the path of the shelf corner. A closed ring box and a blank invoice share the ledge between JUCA and the groom. TEO (frame left): tall thin white clay man, huge straw-blond walrus moustache, teal knitted beanie with cream stripes, red-and-black checked flannel shirt, brown suspenders, khaki trousers, dark boots. JUCA (frame right): short wide Black clay man, burnt-brown flat cap, mustard cable-knit sweater, olive-green trousers, pale wooden clogs, pencil behind the right ear. Exactly two clay puppets appear in the frame: TEO stays at frame left and JUCA stays at frame right; no other people or animals appear. AT START: The dark hoop shelf rests on the tall oak block with one corner of its clay heel submerged. JUCA grips the dry right handle with his left hand; TEO measures from the left rim. One tile is wet. The tap is shut and the groom leans beside the open ring box and blank invoice. [Shot 1] Gallery wide. TEO brings one forearm level with the stone sill. JUCA lifts the handle clear of the tall block with his left hand and sets his right thumb against the block's upper corner. [Shot 2] At 00:02.800, the camera cuts to At sill height TEO brings his other forearm down toward the first. JUCA tips the block outward with his right thumb until its broad face strikes the dry sill. With his left hand he lowers the shelf onto the shorter support. The bolted hinge turns, the clay heel enters deeper and water folds over the same front lip. [Shot 3] At 00:07.000, the camera cuts to Widen to include the grout seam. Water drops into the first wet patch and crosses the seam onto the adjoining tile. JUCA spreads his right fingertips against the exposed side of the block. The groom lifts his low shoulder a little as the hoops come closer to upright. They do not speak and their mouths do not move, but they breathe, swallow and react with their whole bodies. AT END: The flat oak block props the dark hoop shelf just above level. JUCA grips the dry handle with his left hand and touches the block with his right. TEO measures from the left. Two tiles are wet, the tap is shut and the groom leans slightly beside the open ring box and blank invoice.
overall_soundscape: The iron hinge squeaks briefly on the lift; an oak corner rasps against stone during the tip; the broad wooden face claps flat against the sill; the shelf edge taps oak softly at the new height; water splashes across the tile seam in a short patter; JUCA gives one soft sigh as his arm eases.
non_diegetic_music: Plucked double bass marks two even beats; a quiet viola answers half a beat late.
